title: Compliance Intake Traffic Director and Evidence Bundler
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and procurement teams submit a wide variety of security and compliance requests (SOC2/ISO attestation checks, HIPAA controls, GDPR/DPA clauses, and lengthy vendor questionnaires). Today these requests route inconsistently across security, legal, and product, causing slow SLA responses (>10 business days), duplicate work, and poor visibility for account teams.

Goal: Build a lightweight Compliance Intake Traffic Director that programmatically classifies incoming asks, applies a clear SLA tier (auto, concierge, legal review), and assembles a contextual evidence bundle for each request. This reduces mean time to first response to under 48 hours for low/medium requests, surface urgent blockers for security/legal within 4 hours, and creates audit-ready artifacts for recurring questionnaire items.

Scope:
- Inbound channels: Support (Zendesk), Sales/CS (Intercom links), Manual intake form, and direct emails to compliance@redwood.com.
- Classification: Auto-detect request type (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaire, audit request) and confidence score.
- Routing policy: Map classification + customer tier + requested SLA to lane: Auto (self-serve evidence bundle), Security review (SRE/Sec owner), Legal review (contracts/legal), or Escalation (exec/infra).
- Evidence bundler: Pre-assembled artifact sets (SOC2 package, encryption/KMS proof steps, Datacenter maps, DPIAs) plus links to PRs/dashboards, and a single downloadable zip.
- Telemetry: track TTFR, handoffs, and reassignments for dashboarding in Console.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Incoming samples from last 90 days classify into a lane with >85% precision on a held-out set.
2) Auto-lane responses generated with a curated evidence bundle in under 10 minutes.
3) SLA tags applied and visible in intake UI and Zendesk ticket in first response.
4) Hand-off to Security/Legal includes a prefilled summary, templates for required actions, and list of missing evidence.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to first response: target 48 hours (low/med), 4 hours (high).
- Reduction in manual triage tasks for security from 35% to <10% of weekly workload.
- Customer satisfaction for compliance requests (post-resolution NPS-style) improves by 15 points.

Design/implementation notes:
- Use a rule-first approach initially: regexes + keyword mapping + small classifier model for vendor questionnaires. Replace with ML hybrid if accuracy lags.
- Evidence bundles are versioned artifacts stored in Drive/Confluence with stable IDs and audit log.
- Integrations: Zendesk (ticket updates + attachments), Intercom (conversation threads), Google Drive (evidence), GitHub (link to infra PRs), and Console for metrics.
- Security: evidence bundles must respect data residency flags (do not include PII or customer-specific logs in auto bundles).

Risks and mitigations:
- Legal nuance: Some DPAs require bespoke redlines — route to Legal lane and provide a fast-path templating engine.
- False positives on classification: keep an easy override and feedback loop to retrain rules.
- Operational overhead for maintaining evidence items: create an ownership matrix and quarterly review cadence.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal CS + sales only (2 weeks) - rule-only classification + manual evidence selection.
2) Beta: select enterprise customers (4 weeks) - add auto-bundling for SOC2/DPA + metrics.
3) GA: all customers (2 months) - full channel integrations and SLA enforcement.
